greek: τοῦ ἔχειν μὲν αἷμα τὸν φανησόμενον, ἀλλ᾽ οὐκ ἐξ ἀνθρωπείου σπέρματος ἀλλ᾽ ἐκ ϑείας δυνάμεως. Ἡ δὲ πρώτη δύναμις μετὰ τὸν πατέρα πάντων καὶ δεσπότην ϑεὸν καὶ υἱὸς ὁ λόγος ἐστίν· ὃς τίνα τρόπον σαρκοποιηϑεὶς ἄνϑρωπος γέγονεν, ἐν τοῖς ἑξῆς ἐροῦμεν.
greek_edition: Rauschen 1911, read from the archive.org scan (PDF text layer), with page images checked where status is VERIFIED. Rauschen's printed theta (U+03D1) is kept. Section numbers are Rauschen's (= Otto's sections as printed).
english: And the first power after God the Father and Lord of all is the Word, who is also the Son; and of Him we will, in what follows, relate how He took flesh and became man.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts and Donaldson)
page: Rauschen 1911 printed p. 64 (PDF p. 72); English page unknown (New Advent web text, printed ANF page not seen).
edition: Greek: Rauschen 1911 (Florilegium II). English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (publisher and year not shown on the New Advent page)
what_it_says: Justin calls the Word the first power after God the Father and Lord of all and, in the same clause, identifies that Word as the Son.
limits: The objection is the ordering ('after the Father') and the word 'power' (δύναμις), which Arians and Unitarians read as an attribute. The clause does give the Son identity, but says nothing on eternity, equality or the Spirit. Rauschen's footnote 1 on this page (Latin: 'Vide, quae supra p. 26 adn. 3 de subordinatianismo S. Iustini disputavi') says he had already treated Justin's subordinationism. The brief's wording ('first Power after the Father and Lord of all, and Son, is the Word') is not the ANF wording.

ref: 1 Apol. 33.4 (Rauschen/Otto sections; ANF ch. 33; Luke 1:35 is cited)
greek: Τὸ οὖν „Ἰδοὺ ἡ παρϑένος ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει“ σημαίνει οὐ συνουσιασϑεῖσαν τὴν παρϑένον συλλαβεῖν· εἰ γὰρ ἐσυνουσιάσϑη ὑπὸ ὁτιοῦν, οὐκ ἔτι ἦν παρϑένος· ἀλλὰ δύναμις ϑεοῦ ἐπελϑοῦσα τῇ παρϑένῳ ἐπεσκίασεν αὐτήν, καὶ κυοφορῆσαι παρϑένον οὖσαν πεποίηκε.
greek_edition: Rauschen 1911, read from the archive.org scan (PDF text layer), with page images checked where status is VERIFIED. Rauschen's printed theta (U+03D1) is kept. Section numbers are Rauschen's (= Otto's sections as printed).
english: ...For if she had had intercourse with any one whatever, she was no longer a virgin; but the power of God having come upon the virgin, overshadowed her, and caused her while yet a virgin to conceive.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts and Donaldson)
page: Rauschen 1911 printed p. 64 (PDF p. 72); English page unknown (New Advent web text, printed ANF page not seen).
edition: Greek: Rauschen 1911 (Florilegium II). English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (publisher and year not shown on the New Advent page)
what_it_says: Justin explains the conception without intercourse as the power of God coming upon the virgin and overshadowing her.
limits: The agent of conception is 'the power of God' (δύναμις ϑεοῦ), not named as Spirit or Word in this sentence; the identification comes in the next section (J2-03). The Greek text runs from printed p. 64 to p. 66 (PDF 72 to 74); the continuation ἐπελϑοῦσα is on p. 66, checked on the image. The variant 'ὑπὸ ὁτιοῦν' was read from the image and is the least certain word in this item.

greek: Τὸ πνεῦμα οὖν καὶ τὴν δύναμιν τὴν παρὰ τοῦ ϑεοῦ οὐδὲν ἄλλο νοῆσαι ἢ τὸν λόγον, ὃς καὶ πρωτότοκος τῷ ϑεῷ ἐστι, Μωϋσῆς ὁ προδεδηλωμένος προφήτης ἐμήνυσε· καὶ τοῦτο ἐλϑὸν ἐπὶ τὴν παρϑένον καὶ ἐπισκιάσαν οὐ διὰ συνουσίας ἀλλὰ διὰ δυνάμεως ἐγκύμονα κατέστησε.
greek_edition: Rauschen 1911, read from the archive.org scan (PDF text layer), with page images checked where status is VERIFIED. Rauschen's printed theta (U+03D1) is kept. Section numbers are Rauschen's (= Otto's sections as printed).
english: It is wrong, therefore, to understand the Spirit and the power of God as anything else than the Word, who is also the first-born of God, as the foresaid prophet Moses declared; and it was this which, when it came upon the virgin and overshadowed her, caused her to conceive, not by intercourse, but by power.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts and Donaldson)
page: Rauschen 1911 printed p. 66 (PDF p. 74); English page unknown (New Advent web text, printed ANF page not seen).
edition: Greek: Rauschen 1911 (Florilegium II). English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (publisher and year not shown on the New Advent page)
what_it_says: Justin identifies the Spirit and the power of God in Luke 1:35 with nothing other than the Word, who is also the firstborn of God.
limits: Opponents cite this as the Spirit = Word = power. The text gives no separate personal Spirit here. The Greek 'πρωτότοκος τῷ ϑεῷ' repeats the firstborn term of J2-05. Rauschen's footnote 6 on this page (Latin: 'Virtute logi divini, non spiritus sancti, incarnationem dei factam esse et Iust. aliis locis (ex. gr.') says the incarnation is by the Logos, not the Spirit; the footnote is cut off at the page foot. Otto's text reads 'ὡς Μωϋσῆς' (footnote b).

greek: Ὅταν δὲ τὰς λέξεις τῶν προφητῶν λεγομένας ὡς ἀπὸ προσώπου ἀκούητε, μὴ ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν τῶν ἐμπεπνευσμένων λέγεσϑαι νομίσητε, ἀλλ᾽ ἀπὸ τοῦ κινοῦντος αὐτοὺς ϑείου λόγου. Ποτὲ μὲν γὰρ ὡς προαγγελτικῶς τὰ μέλλοντα γενήσεσϑαι λέγει, ποτὲ δὲ ὡς ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ δεσπότου πάντων καὶ πατρὸς ϑεοῦ φϑέγγεται, ποτὲ δὲ ὡς ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ποτὲ δὲ ὡς ἀπὸ προσώπου λαῶν ἀποκρινομένων τῷ κυρίῳ ἢ τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ.
greek_edition: Rauschen 1911, read from the archive.org scan (PDF text layer), with page images checked where status is VERIFIED. Rauschen's printed theta (U+03D1) is kept. Section numbers are Rauschen's (= Otto's sections as printed).
english: But when you hear the utterances of the prophets spoken as it were personally, you must not suppose that they are spoken by the inspired themselves, but by the Divine Word who moves them. For sometimes He declares things that are to come to pass, in the manner of one who foretells the future; sometimes He speaks as from the person of God the Lord and Father of all; sometimes as from the person of Christ; sometimes as from the person of the people answering the Lord or His Father,
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts and Donaldson)
page: Rauschen 1911 printed p. 68 (PDF p. 76); English page unknown (New Advent web text, printed ANF page not seen).
edition: Greek: Rauschen 1911 (Florilegium II). English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (publisher and year not shown on the New Advent page)
what_it_says: The Divine Word moves the prophets and speaks through them, sometimes in the person of God the Father and sometimes in the person of Christ.
limits: This explains prophetic speech in the first person of God or Christ, so it answers the claim that the Father speaks at every prophecy. It does not define the Word's relation to the Father or say he is God in these lines. The 'person' (ἀπὸ προσώπου) is a speaking role, which a critic can read as a modalist claim. Read from the text layer of the scan; not checked on the page image.

greek: Τὸν Χριστὸν πρωτότοκον τοῦ ϑεοῦ εἶναι ἐδιδάχϑημεν καὶ προεμηνύσαμεν λόγον ὄντα, οὗ πᾶν γένος ἀνϑρώπων μετέσχε. Καὶ οἱ μετὰ λόγου βιώσαντες Χριστιανοὶ εἰσι, κἂν ἄϑεοι ἐνομίσϑησαν.
greek_edition: Rauschen 1911, read from the archive.org scan (PDF text layer), with page images checked where status is VERIFIED. Rauschen's printed theta (U+03D1) is kept. Section numbers are Rauschen's (= Otto's sections as printed).
english: We have been taught that Christ is the first-born of God, and we have declared above that He is the Word of whom every race of men were partakers; and those who lived reasonably are Christians, even though they have been thought atheists;
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts and Donaldson)
page: Rauschen 1911 printed p. 80 (PDF p. 88); English page unknown (New Advent web text, printed ANF page not seen).
edition: Greek: Rauschen 1911 (Florilegium II). English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (publisher and year not shown on the New Advent page)
what_it_says: Justin says Christ is the firstborn of God and the Word in whom every race of men partook, so the Word was active before the incarnation.
limits: This is the 'temporal generation' worry: 'firstborn' (πρωτότοκος) suggests a beginning. The Greek gives the Word as 'being' (ὄντα) before the incarnation but says nothing about eternity, and no sentence here says 'before all ages'. The same chapter (46.5) gives the incarnation's cause as power and will (J2-06).

greek: Δι᾽ ἣν αἰτίαν διὰ δυνάμεως τοῦ λόγου κατὰ τὴν τοῦ πατρὸς πάντων καὶ δεσπότου ϑεοῦ βουλὴν διὰ παρϑένου ἄνϑρωπος ἀπεκυήϑη καὶ Ἰησοῦς ἐπωνομάσϑη, καὶ σταυρωϑεὶς καὶ ἀποϑανὼν ἀνέστη καὶ ἀνελήλυϑεν εἰς οὐρανόν, ἐκ τῶν διὰ τοσούτων εἰρημένων ὁ νουνεχὴς καταλαβεῖν δυνήσεται.
greek_edition: Rauschen 1911, read from the archive.org scan (PDF text layer), with page images checked where status is VERIFIED. Rauschen's printed theta (U+03D1) is kept. Section numbers are Rauschen's (= Otto's sections as printed).
english: But who, through the power of the Word, according to the will of God the Father and Lord of all, He was born of a virgin as a man, and was named Jesus, and was crucified, and died, and rose again, and ascended into heaven, an intelligent man will be able to comprehend from what has been already so largely said.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts and Donaldson)
page: Rauschen 1911 printed p. 80 (PDF p. 88); English page unknown (New Advent web text, printed ANF page not seen).
edition: Greek: Rauschen 1911 (Florilegium II). English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (publisher and year not shown on the New Advent page)
what_it_says: The birth of the man Jesus from a virgin happened through the power of the Word, by the will (βουλή) of the Father.
limits: This answers the 'power and will' objection by putting the Word's power as the means and the Father's counsel as the cause, and by speaking of the man born, not of the Word's being. It does not say when the Word began, nor does it treat the Word as created. ANF renders βουλή as 'will' here and as 'counsel' in 63.16 (J2-15); the Greek word is the same.

greek: Τίνι γὰρ ἂν λόγῳ ἀνϑρώπῳ σταυρωϑέντι ἐπειϑόμεϑα, ἔτι πρωτότοκος τῷ ἀγεννήτῳ ϑεῷ ἐστι καὶ αὐτὸς τὴν κρίσιν τοῦ παντὸς ἀνϑρωπείου γένους ποιήσεται.
greek_edition: Rauschen 1911, read from the archive.org scan (PDF text layer), with page images checked where status is VERIFIED. Rauschen's printed theta (U+03D1) is kept. Section numbers are Rauschen's (= Otto's sections as printed).
english: For with what reason should we believe of a crucified man that He is the first-born of the unbegotten God, and Himself will pass judgment on the whole human race
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts and Donaldson)
page: Rauschen 1911 printed p. 88 (PDF p. 96); English page unknown (New Advent web text, printed ANF page not seen).
edition: Greek: Rauschen 1911 (Florilegium II). English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (publisher and year not shown on the New Advent page)
what_it_says: Justin asks why anyone would believe that a crucified man is the firstborn of the unbegotten God and the future judge of all humanity.
limits: This is the most direct 'firstborn of the unbegotten God' sentence in the range 31-68, and it makes the Son a judge (a divine office). The text sets 'unbegotten' (ἀγέννητος) against the Son's derived status without explaining the relation. It is a prophecy-based argument, not a metaphysical one, and the next clause (unless testimonies had been given beforehand) is not quoted here.

greek: Ἀναγνοὺς Πλάτων καὶ μὴ ἀκριβῶς ἐπιστάμενος, μηδὲ νοήσας τύπον εἶναι σταυροῦ ἀλλὰ χίασμα νοήσας, τὴν μετὰ τὸν πρῶτον ϑεὸν δύναμιν κεχιάσϑαι ἐν τῷ παντὶ εἶπε. Καὶ τὸ εἰπεῖν αὐτὸν τρίτον, ἐπειδή, ὡς προείπομεν, ἐπάνω τῶν ὑδάτων ἀνέγνω ὑπὸ Μωϋσέως εἰρημένον ἐπιφέρεσϑαι τὸ τοῦ ϑεοῦ πνεῦμα· δευτέραν μὲν γὰρ χώραν τῷ παρὰ ϑεοῦ λόγῳ, ὃν κεχιάσϑαι ἐν τῷ παντὶ ἔφη, δίδωσι, τὴν δὲ τρίτην τῷ λεχϑέντι ἐπιφέρεσϑαι τῷ ὕδατι πνεύματι, εἰπών· „Τὰ δὲ τρίτα περὶ τὸν τρίτον“.
greek_edition: Rauschen 1911, read from the archive.org scan (PDF text layer), with page images checked where status is VERIFIED. Rauschen's printed theta (U+03D1) is kept. Section numbers are Rauschen's (= Otto's sections as printed).
english: ...he said that the power next to the first God was placed crosswise in the universe. And as to his speaking of a third, he did this because he read, as we said above, that which was spoken by Moses, that the Spirit of God moved over the waters. For he gives the second place to the Logos which is with God, who he said was placed crosswise in the universe; and the third place to the Spirit who was said to be borne upon the water, saying, And the third around the third.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts and Donaldson)
page: Rauschen 1911 printed p. 96 (PDF p. 104); English page unknown (New Advent web text, printed ANF page not seen).
edition: Greek: Rauschen 1911 (Florilegium II). English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (publisher and year not shown on the New Advent page)
what_it_says: Justin reads Plato's 'second' and 'third' as the Logos (second, with God) and the Spirit (third), taken from Moses' creation account.
limits: This is the 'second and third' order that critics cite. It is Justin's reading of Plato (an exegetical claim about Plato's text), not a dogmatic definition of rank. The Greek calls the Logos 'the power after the first God' (60.5) and then 'the second place' (60.7). Justin does not say 'equal' or 'consubstantial'. Used by critics as ranking; read as an exegetical claim about Timaeus.

greek: Ἔπειτα ἄγονται ὑφ᾽ ἡμῶν, ἔνϑα ὕδωρ ἐστί, καὶ τρόπον ἀναγεννήσεως, ὃν καὶ ἡμεῖς αὐτοὶ ἀνεγεννήϑημεν, ἀναγεννῶνται· ἐπ᾽ ὀνόματος γὰρ τοῦ πατρὸς τῶν ὅλων καὶ δεσπότου ϑεοῦ καὶ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ πνεύματος ἁγίου τὸ ἐν τῷ ὕδατι τότε λουτρὸν ποιοῦνται.
greek_edition: Rauschen 1911, read from the archive.org scan (PDF text layer), with page images checked where status is VERIFIED. Rauschen's printed theta (U+03D1) is kept. Section numbers are Rauschen's (= Otto's sections as printed).
english: For, in the name of God, the Father and Lord of the universe, and of our Saviour Jesus Christ, and of the Holy Spirit, they then receive the washing with water.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts and Donaldson)
page: Rauschen 1911 printed p. 98 (PDF p. 106); English page unknown (New Advent web text, printed ANF page not seen).
edition: Greek: Rauschen 1911 (Florilegium II). English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (publisher and year not shown on the New Advent page)
what_it_says: Candidates are baptized in the name of the Father (God and Lord of the universe), of Jesus Christ and of the Holy Spirit.
limits: The three names are joined under one 'name' (ὀνόματος, singular) and the Father is called 'God' and 'Lord of the universe'. The Spirit is named with no further description in this sentence, and there is no statement of equality or consubstantiality. The page carries an editor's footnote calling the rite a 'consecratio' that happens with baptism and eucharist (Latin, image of p. 98).

greek: Καὶ ἐπ᾽ ὀνόματος δὲ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ σταυρωϑέντος ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου, καὶ ἐπ᾽ ὀνόματος πνεύματος ἁγίου, ὃ διὰ τῶν προφητῶν προεκήρυξε τὰ κατὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν πάντα, ὁ φωτιζόμενος λούεται.
greek_edition: Rauschen 1911, read from the archive.org scan (PDF text layer), with page images checked where status is VERIFIED. Rauschen's printed theta (U+03D1) is kept. Section numbers are Rauschen's (= Otto's sections as printed).
english: And in the name of Jesus Christ, who was crucified under Pontius Pilate, and in the name of the Holy Ghost, who through the prophets foretold all things about Jesus, he who is illuminated is washed.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts and Donaldson)
page: Rauschen 1911 printed p. 100 (PDF p. 108); English page unknown (New Advent web text, printed ANF page not seen).
edition: Greek: Rauschen 1911 (Florilegium II). English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (publisher and year not shown on the New Advent page)
what_it_says: The one illuminated is washed in the name of Jesus Christ and in the name of the Holy Spirit, who through the prophets proclaimed everything about Jesus.
limits: The Spirit is the speaker of the prophecies; that is a role, not a statement of divinity. The Greek is a list of names in a baptismal formula, not a doctrine of three persons. Justin does not call the Spirit God in this section.

greek: Ὁ λόγος δὲ τοῦ ϑεοῦ ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ, ὡς προέφημεν. Καὶ ἄγγελος δὲ καλεῖται καὶ ἀπόστολος· αὐτὸς γὰρ ἀπαγγέλλει, ὅσα δεῖ γνωσϑῆναι, καὶ ἀποστέλλεται κηρύσσων, ὅσα ἀγγέλλεται, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν εἶπεν· „Ὁ ἐμοῦ ἀκούων ἀκούει τοῦ ἀποστείλαντός με“.
greek_edition: Rauschen 1911, read from the archive.org scan (PDF text layer), with page images checked where status is VERIFIED. Rauschen's printed theta (U+03D1) is kept. Section numbers are Rauschen's (= Otto's sections as printed).
english: Now the Word of God is His Son, as we have before said. And He is called Angel and Apostle; for He declares whatever we ought to know, and is sent forth to declare whatever is revealed; as our Lord Himself says, He that hears Me, hears Him that sent Me.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts and Donaldson)
page: Rauschen 1911 printed p. 102 (PDF p. 110); English page unknown (New Advent web text, printed ANF page not seen).
edition: Greek: Rauschen 1911 (Florilegium II). English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (publisher and year not shown on the New Advent page)
what_it_says: Justin says the Word of God is the Son and is called 'angel' and 'apostle' because he is the one who declares and is sent to declare.
limits: The title 'angel' is a function (messenger, 'declares'), which answers the claim that 'angel' means a created being. It also says the Son is 'sent' (ἀποστέλλεται) by the one who sent him, which critics read as subordination; the Greek does not say whether the sending is temporal. The ANF's 'Angel' capitalization is the translator's.

greek: Ἀλλ᾽ εἰς ἀπόδειξιν γεγόνασιν οἵδε οἱ λόγοι, ὅτι υἱὸς ϑεοῦ καὶ ἀπόστολος Ἰησοῦς ὁ Χριστός ἐστι, πρότερον λόγος ὤν, καὶ ἐν ἰδέᾳ πυρὸς ποτὲ φανείς, ποτὲ δὲ καὶ ἐν εἰκόνι ἀσωμάτῳ· νῦν δὲ διὰ ϑελήματος ϑεοῦ ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἀνϑρωπείου γένους ἄνϑρωπος γενόμενος ὑπέμεινε καὶ παϑεῖν, ὅσα αὐτὸν ἐνήργησαν οἱ δαίμονες διατεϑῆναι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνοήτων Ἰουδαίων.
greek_edition: Rauschen 1911, read from the archive.org scan (PDF text layer), with page images checked where status is VERIFIED. Rauschen's printed theta (U+03D1) is kept. Section numbers are Rauschen's (= Otto's sections as printed).
english: But so much is written for the sake of proving that Jesus the Christ is the Son of God and His Apostle, being of old the Word, and appearing sometimes in the form of fire, and sometimes in the likeness of angels; but now, by the will of God, having become man for the human race, He endured all the sufferings which the devils instigated the senseless Jews to inflict upon Him
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts and Donaldson)
page: Rauschen 1911 printed p. 102 (PDF p. 110); English page unknown (New Advent web text, printed ANF page not seen).
edition: Greek: Rauschen 1911 (Florilegium II). English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (publisher and year not shown on the New Advent page)
what_it_says: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Apostle, was the Word before, appeared in fire and in an incorporeal form, and by God's will became man for the human race.
limits: It states pre-existence ('being of old the Word') and calls the Son God's Son. Limits: the ANF renders εἰκόνι ἀσωμάτῳ ('incorporeal likeness') as 'likeness of angels', which is not in the Greek; the Greek says 'by the will of God' (ϑελήματος), the same will-language as J2-06. The Son's appearances in fire are a theophany argument (J2-13, J2-14).

greek: Οἵτινες ἔχοντες ῥητῶς εἰρημένον ἐν τοῖς Μωϋσέως συντάγμασι· „Καὶ ἐλάλησεν ἄγγελος τοῦ ϑεοῦ τῷ Μωϋσεῖ ἐν πυρὶ φλογὸς ἐν βάτῳ καὶ εἶπεν· „Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν, ὁ ϑεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ ϑεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ ϑεὸς Ἰακώβ“,, τὸν τῶν ὅλων πατέρα καὶ δημιουργὸν ταῦτα εἰπόντα λέγουσιν εἶναι.
greek_edition: Rauschen 1911, read from the archive.org scan (PDF text layer), with page images checked where status is VERIFIED. Rauschen's printed theta (U+03D1) is kept. Section numbers are Rauschen's (= Otto's sections as printed).
english: ...though they have it expressly affirmed in the writings of Moses, And the angel of God spoke to Moses in a flame of fire in a bush, and said, I am that I am, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, yet maintain that He who said this was the Father and Creator of the universe.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts and Donaldson)
page: Rauschen 1911 printed p. 102 (PDF p. 110); English page unknown (New Advent web text, printed ANF page not seen).
edition: Greek: Rauschen 1911 (Florilegium II). English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (publisher and year not shown on the New Advent page)
what_it_says: Justin reports the Jewish reading that the speaker from the bush, quoted as 'the angel of God', was the Father and Creator of all.
limits: This is the opponents' argument as Justin reports it, and it is the burning-bush point the brief asks for. The Greek quotation says 'ἄγγελος τοῦ ϑεοῦ' and 'ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν'. Justin's answer comes in 63.10 and 63.14-15 (J2-12, J2-14). Justin does not quote the opponents' full argument here.

greek: Ἰουδαῖοι οὖν ἡγησάμενοι ἀεὶ τὸν πατέρα τῶν ὅλων λελαληκέναι τῷ Μωϋσεῖ, τοῦ λαλήσαντος αὐτῷ ὄντος υἱοῦ τοῦ ϑεοῦ, ὃς καὶ ἄγγελος καὶ ἀπόστολος κέκληται, δικαίως ἐλέγχονται καὶ διὰ τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος καὶ δι᾽ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὡς οὔτε τὸν πατέρα οὔτε τὸν υἱὸν ἔγνωσαν. Οἱ γὰρ τὸν υἱὸν πατέρα φάσκοντες εἶναι ἐλέγχονται, μήτε τὸν πατέρα ἐπιστάμενοι, μηδ᾽ ὅτι ἐστὶν υἱὸς τῷ πατρὶ τῶν ὅλων γινώσκοντες· ὃς λόγος καὶ πρωτότοκος ὢν τοῦ ϑεοῦ καὶ ϑεὸς ὑπάρχει.
greek_edition: Rauschen 1911, read from the archive.org scan (PDF text layer), with page images checked where status is VERIFIED. Rauschen's printed theta (U+03D1) is kept. Section numbers are Rauschen's (= Otto's sections as printed).
english: The Jews, accordingly, being throughout of opinion that it was the Father of the universe who spoke to Moses, though He who spoke to him was indeed the Son of God, who is called both Angel and Apostle, are justly charged, both by the Spirit of prophecy and by Christ Himself, with knowing neither the Father nor the Son. For they who affirm that the Son is the Father, are proved neither to have become acquainted with the Father, nor to know that the Father of the universe has a Son; who also, being the first-begotten Word of God, is even God.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts and Donaldson)
page: Rauschen 1911 printed p. 104 (PDF p. 112); English page unknown (New Advent web text, printed ANF page not seen).
edition: Greek: Rauschen 1911 (Florilegium II). English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (publisher and year not shown on the New Advent page)
what_it_says: The Son of God, the first-begotten Word, is God, and those who call the Son the Father do not know the Father of the universe.
limits: This is the clearest 'God' statement for the Word in this range: 'ϑεὸς ὑπάρχει'. Limits: the predicate is said of the Word (ὃς λόγος), not 'Jesus' and not 'the same God'; there is no ὁμοούσιος or 'true God' language; 'first-born' (πρωτότοκος) is again the firstborn term; the Father/Son distinction is explicit. The relative pronoun reads 'ὃς' here; the image is at the limit of legibility (ὡς possible), see notes.

greek: Καὶ πρότερον διὰ τῆς τοῦ πυρὸς μορφῆς καὶ εἰκόνος ἀσωμάτου τῷ Μωϋσεῖ καὶ τοῖς ἑτέροις προφήταις ἐφάνη· νῦν δ᾽ ἐν χρόνοις τῆς ὑμετέρας ἀρχῆς, ὡς προείπομεν, διὰ παρϑένου ἄνϑρωπος γενόμενος κατὰ τὴν τοῦ πατρὸς βουλὴν ὑπὲρ σωτηρίας τῶν πιστευόντων αὐτῷ καὶ ἐξουϑενηϑῆναι καὶ παϑεῖν ὑπέμεινεν. Τὸ δὲ εἰρημένον ἐκ βάτου τῷ Μωϋσεῖ· „Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν, ὁ ϑεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ ϑεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ ϑεὸς Ἰακὼβ καὶ ὁ ϑεὸς τῶν πατέρων σου“, σημαντικὸν τοῦ καὶ ἀποϑανόντας ἐκείνους μένειν καὶ εἶναι αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀνϑρώπους.
greek_edition: Rauschen 1911, read from the archive.org scan (PDF text layer), with page images checked where status is VERIFIED. Rauschen's printed theta (U+03D1) is kept. Section numbers are Rauschen's (= Otto's sections as printed).
english: And of old He appeared in the shape of fire and in the likeness of an angel to Moses and to the other prophets; but now in the times of your reign, having, as we before said, become Man by a virgin, according to the counsel of the Father, for the salvation of those who believe in Him, He endured both to be set at nought and to suffer, ... And that which was said out of the bush to Moses, I am that I am, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, and the God of your fathers, Exodus 3:6 this signified that they, even though dead, are yet in existence, and are men belonging to Christ Himself.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts and Donaldson)
page: Rauschen 1911 printed p. 104 (PDF p. 112); English page unknown (New Advent web text, printed ANF page not seen).
edition: Greek: Rauschen 1911 (Florilegium II). English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (publisher and year not shown on the New Advent page)
what_it_says: The Word appeared of old in fire and in an incorporeal form, and in these last times became man by a virgin according to the Father's counsel; the bush words show the patriarchs live.
limits: Opponents use the theophanies and the 'counsel of the Father' to make the Son an instrument of the Father. Justin's reply is that the one who appeared in fire is the one who became man (same subject). The sentence on the patriarchs living is an argument for the resurrection, not for the Son's rank. ANF renders εἰκόνος ἀσωμάτου as 'likeness of an angel' (not in the Greek), and βουλή as 'counsel' here but 'will' in J2-06.

greek: Ἔπειτα προσφέρεται τῷ προεστῶτι τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἄρτος καὶ ποτήριον ὕδατος καὶ κράματος· καὶ οὗτος λαβὼν αἶνον καὶ δόξαν τῷ πατρὶ τῶν ὅλων διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου ἀναπέμπει καὶ εὐχαριστίαν ὑπὲρ τοῦ καταξιωϑῆναι τούτων παρ᾽ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πολὺ ποιεῖται.
greek_edition: Rauschen 1911, read from the archive.org scan (PDF text layer), with page images checked where status is VERIFIED. Rauschen's printed theta (U+03D1) is kept. Section numbers are Rauschen's (= Otto's sections as printed).
english: There is then brought to the president of the brethren bread and a cup of wine mixed with water; and he taking them, gives praise and glory to the Father of the universe, through the name of the Son and of the Holy Ghost, and offers thanks at considerable length for our being counted worthy to receive these things at His hands.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts and Donaldson)
page: Rauschen 1911 printed p. 106 (PDF p. 114); English page unknown (New Advent web text, printed ANF page not seen).
edition: Greek: Rauschen 1911 (Florilegium II). English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (publisher and year not shown on the New Advent page)
what_it_says: At the Eucharist the presider gives praise to the Father of the universe through the name of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
limits: The liturgical pattern is Father, then Son and Spirit as the means of praise; that is a worship pattern, not a doctrinal statement. The praise is addressed to the Father only. The Greek 'διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος' gives the name as the instrument for both the Son and the Spirit.

greek: Οὐ γὰρ ὡς κοινὸν ἄρτον οὐδὲ κοινὸν πόμα ταῦτα λαμβάνομεν· ἀλλ᾽ ὃν τρόπον διὰ λόγου ϑεοῦ σαρκοποιηϑεὶς Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ὁ σωτὴρ ἡμῶν καὶ σάρκα καὶ αἷμα ὑπὲρ σωτηρίας ἡμῶν ἔσχεν, οὕτως καὶ τὴν δι᾽ εὐχῆς λόγου τοῦ παρ᾽ αὐτοῦ εὐχαριστηϑεῖσαν τροφήν, ἐξ ἧς αἷμα καὶ σάρκες κατὰ μεταβολὴν τρέφονται ἡμῶν, ἐκείνου τοῦ σαρκοποιηϑέντος Ἰησοῦ καὶ σάρκα καὶ αἷμα ἐδιδάχϑημεν εἶναι.

english: ...but in like manner as Jesus Christ our Saviour, having been made flesh by the Word of God, had both flesh and blood for our salvation, so likewise have we been taught that the food which is blessed by the prayer of His word, and from which our blood and flesh by transmutation are nourished, is the flesh and blood of that Jesus who was made flesh.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts and Donaldson)
page: Rauschen 1911 printed p. 108 (PDF p. 116); English page unknown (New Advent web text, printed ANF page not seen).
edition: Greek: Rauschen 1911 (Florilegium II). English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (publisher and year not shown on the New Advent page)
what_it_says: Jesus Christ, made flesh through the Word of God, had flesh and blood, and the eucharistic food is the flesh and blood of that incarnate Jesus.
limits: The Word of God is the agent of the incarnation ('made flesh by the Word of God'). The Greek does not say 'God the Word' here, and 'λόγος ϑεοῦ' can be read as an impersonal word. The passage is about the Eucharist, so it does not settle the Word's nature.

greek: Ἐπὶ πᾶσί τε οἷς προσφερόμεϑα εὐλογοῦμεν τὸν ποιητὴν τῶν πάντων διὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ διὰ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου.
greek_edition: Rauschen 1911, read from the archive.org scan (PDF text layer), with page images checked where status is VERIFIED. Rauschen's printed theta (U+03D1) is kept. Section numbers are Rauschen's (= Otto's sections as printed).
english: ...for all things wherewith we are supplied, we bless the Maker of all through His Son Jesus Christ, and through the Holy Ghost.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts and Donaldson)
page: Rauschen 1911 printed p. 108 (PDF p. 116); English page unknown (New Advent web text, printed ANF page not seen).
edition: Greek: Rauschen 1911 (Florilegium II). English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (publisher and year not shown on the New Advent page)
what_it_says: Christians bless the Maker of all through the Son Jesus Christ and through the Holy Spirit.
limits: The Maker is named as the object of blessing and the Son and Spirit as the means ('through'), for both alike, so the preposition does not by itself show rank. The Father is not named in this sentence; 'Maker of all' is the Father by implication.
